bugs_found_and_fixed.title: out-of-scope-read-precedes-write false positive on real transcripts
bugs_found_and_fixed.root_cause: Real claude-code Read/Write tool_use blocks always carry absolute file_path values (e.g. /home/lam/.governator/worktrees/<run>/CHANGELOG.md), but allowed.read/forbidden.paths are documented and validated as repository-relative (docs/contracts.md). The Phase 6 starter rule set's own tests only ever synthesized relative-looking Subject strings by hand, so this was never caught: in practice the rule denied nearly every real write-capable surgeon run, because editing a file always means reading it first.
bugs_found_and_fixed.severity: would have blocked essentially all real approved runs under any allowed.read scope narrower than '**'
bugs_found_and_fixed.fix: auditTranscript now takes the run's worktree path and relativizes a Read/Write event's Subject against it before matching allowed.read, only when the absolute path actually falls under the worktree. An absolute read genuinely outside the worktree (or outside allowed.read) still denies; secret-pattern matching (rule 1) is untouched.

bugs_found_and_fixed.title: codex CLI startup banner treated as transcript corruption
bugs_found_and_fixed.found_via: job v14-session1-safe-fallback, live codex attempt (run agent=codex, ~16:12 UTC)
bugs_found_and_fixed.root_cause: codex exec --json --ephemeral prints a plain-text 'Reading additional input from stdin...' notice on stdout before its first JSON event (real codex CLI behavior). auditTranscript's line-by-line JSONL parser flagged that line as malformed JSON, and on_violation: quarantine turned it into a POLICY_VIOLATION on every single codex-backed run, regardless of what the agent actually did.
bugs_found_and_fixed.severity: blocked every real codex-backed approved run
bugs_found_and_fixed.fix: Only forgive a malformed line seen BEFORE the first valid JSON line (CLI startup noise, which cannot have encoded a tool_use/tool_result event either way); a malformed line after the JSON stream has started still fails closed exactly as before.
bugs_found_and_fixed.regression_test: TestAuditTranscriptTolerantOfLeadingCLIBanner (internal/runtime/transcript_test.go); TestAuditTranscriptRejectsMalformedJSONL (pre-existing) reconfirmed to still fail closed on genuine mid-stream corruption

3_blocking_assayer_quarantine.notes: Agent wrote a real produced artifact (.governator/artifacts/note.json) containing a deliberate TODO placeholder; the real Assayer subprocess evaluated it under the coding-output-v1 profile (blocking enforcement) and correctly failed it.

primary_evidence.description: Fully organic, zero synthetic stubs: real codex attempt hit a genuine QUOTA_EXHAUSTED infra failure with zero mutation; the runtime's own fallback loop automatically retried with claude-code.

attempt_1.verified_preconditions: infra taxonomy + zero tool_calls + unchanged worktree (fallback_attempts row + runs.notes=fallback_worktree_unchanged)

attempt_2.outcome: the overall run still ended QUARANTINED (POLICY_VIOLATION, an unrelated allowed.execute scope gap in this job's contract) but the fallback retry itself is fully proven by the fallback_attempts ledger rows

supplementary_evidence_clean_end_to_end.description: Deterministic stub backends (GOV_CLAUDE_BIN/GOV_CODEX_BIN env overrides, run through the real gov run CLI and full governance pipeline — worktree, ledger, merge gate, route broker) used to force a clean APPROVED-via-fallback outcome, since live backend health kept shifting mid-session (codex genuinely recovered partway through, changing routing scores) and the router's own design prefers not to re-attempt a backend the breaker or scoring has already marked unhealthy.
supplementary_evidence_clean_end_to_end.ledger_verified: runs table: 2 rows (QUARANTINED then APPROVED); fallback_attempts table: 2 rows, attempt 1 reason=RATE_LIMIT, attempt 2 reason=''

5_fallback_refusal_after_mutation.notes: Stub wrote a stray line to CHANGELOG.md, then failed with a RATE_LIMIT infra signature — same taxonomy as the safe-fallback case, but this time with a real prior mutation. fallbackEligible() correctly refused to retry: ledger shows exactly 1 run row and 0 fallback_attempts rows for this job_id, versus 2/2 for the safe-fallback-stub case above. claude-code was available and would have succeeded (as proven by the sibling test) but was never attempted.
5_fallback_refusal_after_mutation.why_stubs_here_too: Same live-routing-drift reason as category 4: by this point in the session codex had accumulated a stronger ledger-scored track record than claude-code and was winning the broker's pick outright, so the stub roles were swapped to match, keeping the test on the real gov run CLI rather than fighting the (correctly) self-correcting scorer.

7_stale_run_recovery.procedure: Launched gov run in the background, confirmed via direct ledger query it reached stage AGENT_RUNNING with status RUNNING, then SIGKILLed the gov process tree (parent + detached child) to simulate a real crash, then ran gov run recover --stale.
7_stale_run_recovery.recovery_result: run_id / action=safe_resume / detail='worktree unchanged since agent launch'
7_stale_run_recovery.notes: Confirms the AGENT_RUNNING checkpoint's worktree-digest mechanism correctly distinguished 'agent never touched the worktree' from a mid-edit crash.
